note: issues, questions and enhancement requests from the panel (Open Items / Roadmap tabs), copied by the nightly; the review answers here and the panel reads it back

items.text: Top 3 or top 5 gamma lines per book? (operator, 2026-09-08: 'is it sufficient to have the top 3 instead of the top 5' — 'record and let me know in about a week from now.. keep it as an open item')
items.answer: Open until ~2026-09-15. The 09-08 hand read (34 taps): ranks 1–3 deflected 15 of 22 with no break; ranks 4–5 3 of 12 with all three breaks; both HODs, the ES LOD and 8 of 10 circled pullbacks had a top-3 line — the gap is the +γ node under a −γ King (rank 4–6). He keeps 5 until the week's table is in.

items.text: The NQ symbol's four QQQ lines in the IRT file — keep G2–G5, or QG2–QG5 to match XG / SG? (asked 2026-09-08 with v15.85)
items.answer: His word, 2026-09-09: "there should be no qqq lines in es. for NQ, just use G because we dont have to distinguish it like for the es which has both spy and spx." — G2–G5 stay on the NQ symbol (one book, nothing to distinguish); the ES file carries no QQQ line (as since v15.80, xqWhy). No build.

items.text: AHI · ALO · LHI · LLO — the session hours: Asia 17:00–02:00 CT and London 02:00–08:30 CT are proposed; his word decides before they draw (locked item, not built)
items.answer: His word 2026-09-09: "just use whatever is standard" — Asia 17:00–02:00 CT, London 02:00–08:30 CT (fixed Chicago hours). Built as AHI / ALO / LHI / LLO in v15.88.

items.text: E005: the first-hour turns he did not circle (ES 08:45 · 09:03 at the ONL/LLO sweep · 09:39 · 09:51; the NQ LOD 09:09 at the PDL sweep) — deflections in his sense, or skipped on purpose? The answer sets the boundary of the Learn corpus.
items.answer: His ruling 2026-09-09: "i agree i think you should also tag other hours" — the five uncircled first-hour turns are deflections (E005 m1–m4, E006 m1), tagged by the hour; every leg carries its hour; the pattern table has the hour class (R-3, v15.88).

items.text: THE TAP RECORD (R-25, design/TAP-RECORD.md): one row per tap of an exported line + two controls, scored DEFLECT · PIN · BREAK with mfe / mae / reach / R; his 'yes' to the design — element 1 (the universe and the controls) awaits his call
items.answer: Designed on paper 2026-09-08; roadmap v15.90; built one element at a time on his word; the clean sample starts 2026-09-09 (F-22). His word 2026-09-09 ("your recommendation"): the tap record is the NEXT build, on its own — v15.90, element 1 (the universe + the two controls).

items.text: AHI · ALO · LHI · LLO on the SWEPT line, the day candle and the sweep study (operator, 2026-09-08: 'we should do it. they can be ALO, AHI, LLO, LHI')
items.answer: Built in v15.88: AHI / ALO / LHI / LLO on the candle, the SWEPT line, the read and the H2 table; the NQ chart gets them with companion v1.19.

items.text: The NQ vendor corpus (data/es-1min/NQ TestingData.txt — 188 sessions, TAB-delimited, no header, ISO timestamps) has no parser in tools/study-hodlod.py, so NQ's BASERATES (data/futures/NQ/BASERATES.json) stands on the Yahoo days alone (11 sessions on 2026-09-08). One loader branch (the format is sniffed by tools/model-lodhod.py already) and the NQ E row would have a corpus.
items.answer: Built in v15.88: study-hodlod.py sniffs the tab / ISO format; NQ BASERATES = 188 vendor + the Yahoo days (195 on 09-08), provenance per session; the four overlapping days read side by side (identical clocks and extremes).

items.text: Agenda item 3 — a patch-build tier? Updates are slow because every build re-runs the whole suite (167 files) and ships the whole tree; a patch tier would ship the panel alone with the touched harnesses. His yes / no (operator, 2026-09-08: 'making updates is very slow. is there a lot of unused code…' — measured: no; the time is the suite and the installer).
items.answer: His word 2026-09-09 ("your recommendation"): no patch tier — batch several issues per build so the fixed cost (the suite, the records, the installer, the CDN wait) is paid once per batch. Closed.
